goggles.aeronauticsbigengine.title: Engine:
gui.aeronauticsbigengine.title: Engine Control Unit
aeronauticsbigengine.ponder.engine_overv: The crank line is built along one axis: crank throws, crankshaft pieces, main bearings and a flywheel
A single Power Output goes at one end of the line. This is where the engine feeds the Create network
Every crank throw drives one cylinder: a connecting rod with a piston on top of it
Above each piston: an empty bore lined with cylinder walls, closed by a cylinder head carrying its ports
Finally, place the Engine Control Unit touching any block of the crank line
Right-click it to open the tuning screen, and press Start
The starter cranks the engine, the cylinders fire and the power flows out through the Power Output
aeronauticsbigengine.ponder.engine_cylin: Place a Connecting Rod on a crank throw, pointing away from the crankshaft
Then an Engine Piston on top of the rod, facing the same way
The block above the piston is the bore. It must stay empty: the piston moves into it
Surround the bore with Cylinder Walls on every side
And close it with a Cylinder Head. Its free faces hold the injector, spark plug, intake and exhaust
While running, the piston travels one block: from its own block up into the bore and back
aeronauticsbigengine.ponder.engine_big_b: Pistons placed side by side, up to 3x3, form one big piston driven by a single rod
The bore and the head grow with it. Walls must enclose the whole bore
Torque depends on the moving mass: every kg of piston and rod (Sable mass) adds stress capacity. Heavier pistons, more SU
Big bores also need more air: add extra air intakes, up to one per piston block, for full power
A flywheel adds inertia: the engine revs up slower but shrugs off sudden loads
aeronauticsbigengine.ponder.engine_ports: Fuel Injector (required): holds 1000 mB of fuel. Fill it with Create pipes or a bucket
Spark Plug: without it the cylinder never ignites
Air Intake (required): it needs open air in front of it to breathe
Exhaust: optional, but without it the cylinder only gives about a third of its power
Thick black smoke means a rich mixture: too much fuel for the air
aeronauticsbigengine.ponder.engine_oil.t: Use the Engine Oil Can on the inner faces of the cylinder walls, inside the bore
The oil clings to the walls like a vine. Use the can again to stack up to 3 layers
The piston slides on this film. Every firing slowly wears it away, so top it up from time to time
Without oil, friction rises up to four times: the engine loses power, overheats and finally seizes
Shortcut: use the can on a Cylinder Head to oil every wall of the bore below it at once
Engineer's Goggles on the controller show how well the engine is lubricated
aeronauticsbigengine.ponder.engine_contr: The Engine Control Unit runs the engine. Right-click it to open its screen
Throttle sets the target speed between Idle and Max RPM. A governor adds or removes fuel to hold it
An analog redstone signal can work the throttle too
Fuel limits the charge per cycle. Air/Fuel ratio (about 13:1 for best power) and ignition Advance tune efficiency
Too much advance makes the engine knock: it heats up fast. Back it off when the screen warns you
Assemble (Sable) turns the crankshaft and every piston into Sable sub-levels that really move, driven by servo joints
On an Aeronautics ship, the moving parts push on the ship itself. Disassemble puts every block back in place
Engineer's Goggles show RPM, stress capacity, temperature, oil and fuel
aeronauticsbigengine.ponder.crank_timing: Each crank throw has a crank pin angle: 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees
Right-click a throw with a Wrench to turn its pin by 90 degrees
The pin angle decides when each piston reaches the top. Opposite pins (0 and 180) make pistons move in opposite directions
In a four-stroke engine each cylinder fires once every two turns. In the screen choose Turn 1 or Turn 2 for each cylinder
Auto timing spreads the firings evenly over the 720 degree cycle: a smooth engine with a high balance value
Uneven firing makes the engine shake, and on a ship that shake is passed to the hull
